publisher: Galatzer-Levy, Huang and Bonanno, Clinical Psychology Review 63:41-55 (2018); Leger, Charles and Almeida, Psychological Science 29(8):1283-1290 (2018)
table: Abstracts (PubMed 29902711 and 29553880), read through NCBI E-utilities
title: Documented adult trajectories after a potentially traumatic event, and next-day carryover of a daily stressor
universe: Galatzer-Levy: 67 cases from 54 trajectory studies of adults after potentially traumatic events (bereavement, injury, disaster, combat and others); Leger: 1,155 adults in a nationwide U.S. daily-diary study, 8 consecutive days
geography: Pooled studies (mostly United States and Europe); United States (Leger)
limits: Trajectory shares are of symptom courses (distress, PTSD, depression) on each study's own scale, not the game's stress number; the band reads them as the share still raised six months after the event. They check a town's bereaved people as a whole and never set one person's stress.

resilience.quote: The resilience trajectory was the modal response across studies (average of 65.7% across populations, 95% CI [0.616, 0.698])

nextDayCarryover.quote: Multilevel models indicated that people experience heightened levels of negative affect the day after a minor stressor occurs.

band.measure: share of people bereaved in the year whose stress six months later is still above the day before the death by at least half of its rise
band.from: chronic plus delayed onset: 0.106 + 0.089 = 0.195, interval 0.086 + 0.053 to 0.127 + 0.133
